The given expression can be written as a​2+b​3+c​5a\sqrt{2}+b\sqrt{3}+c\sqrt{5},
where aa, bb, and cc are positive integers.
We are given the expression:
x​6+y​10+z​15+w\sqrt{x\sqrt{6}+y\sqrt{10}+z\sqrt{15}+w}
Squaring the expression to get rid of the outer square root:
(x​6+y​10+z​15+w)=(a​2+b​3+c​5)2(x\sqrt{6}+y\sqrt{10}+z\sqrt{15}+w)=(a\sqrt{2}+b\sqrt{3}+c\sqrt{5})^{2}
Expanding the right side:
(x​6+y​10+z​15+w)=2​a2+3​b2+5​c2+2​a​b​6+2​a​c​10+2​b​c​15+2​a​b​c​30(x\sqrt{6}+y\sqrt{10}+z\sqrt{15}+w)=2a^{2}+3b^{2}+5c^{2}+2ab\sqrt{6}+2ac\sqrt{10}+2bc\sqrt{15}+2abc\sqrt{30}
Comparing the coefficients of 6\sqrt{6}, 10\sqrt{10}, and 15\sqrt{15}:
x=2​a​bx=2ab, y=2​a​cy=2ac, z=2​b​cz=2bc
Also, the constant term ww is:
w=2​a2+3​b2+5​c2w=2a^{2}+3b^{2}+5c^{2}
We know that aa, bb, and cc are positive integers.
From the coefficients of 6\sqrt{6}, 10\sqrt{10}, and 15\sqrt{15}:
x=2​a​bx=2ab, y=2​a​cy=2ac, z=2​b​cz=2bc
We can see that xx, yy, and zz can be expressed as multiples of 2.
Also, the constant term ww is:
w=2​a2+3​b2+5​c2w=2a^{2}+3b^{2}+5c^{2}
Since xx, yy, and zz are multiples of 2, ww must be a multiple of 2 as well.
The least possible values for aa, bb, and cc that satisfy the conditions are:
a=1a=1, b=1b=1, c=1c=1
Substituting these values in:
x=2​a​b=2​(1)​(1)=2x=2ab=2(1)(1)=2
y=2​a​c=2​(1)​(1)=2y=2ac=2(1)(1)=2
z=2​b​c=2​(1)​(1)=2z=2bc=2(1)(1)=2
w=2​a2+3​b2+5​c2=2​(1)2+3​(1)2+5​(1)2=10w=2a^{2}+3b^{2}+5c^{2}=2(1)^{2}+3(1)^{2}+5(1)^{2}=10
However, w=10w=10 is not a multiple of 2 that satisfies the conditions.
